editorial: We spent a little under $800 in Costa Rica, which doesn’t include flights into and out of the country.

categories.title: STAYS
editorial: We enjoyed a super affordable stay ($28 a night) at Monteverde Backpackers.
Our Airbnb in San Jose was a bit more expensive ($42 a night), but it was in a safe-ish neighbourhood close to the downtown area.

categories.title: FOOD
editorial: We spent about $250 on food, which was very reasonable for the amount we ate. The sumptuous casado cost about $10-$12 a meal (back in 2023).

categories.title: EXPERIENCES
editorial: The bulk of our expenses were in this bucket.
We spent about $15 each on the Gold Museum tour and another $7 each on the National Theatre tour in San Jose.
In Monteverde, the ziplining cost about $75 each, while the night walk was $30 each. The entrance to the cloud forest was $25 per person.

categories.title: INTER-CITY TRAVEL
editorial: The bus rides from San Jose to Monteverde were only $7 each, pretty reasonable for a 5-hour ride!

categories.title: MISCELLANEOUS
editorial: Unless things have changed, if you have a USA or Canada visa, you don’t need a separate visa for Costa Rica. One of us didn’t, so that added $30 to our budget.
We spent $25 on Uber within San Jose. Given how unsafe the city is, we don’t recommend walking after sundown.

alternatives.title: What if we had a bigger budget?
editorial: The days in the hostel are etched in our memory. We wouldn’t swap that for fancier lodging.

alternatives.title: What if we had a smaller budget?
editorial: Cut back on the time and money spent in San Jose and move to Monteverde expeditiously.
